key_insight: A transfer learning-based 3D nnU-Net produced the most accurate intracranial artery segmentation on 7T 4D Flow MRI and best preserved downstream hemodynamic measurements.
clinical_relevance: More reliable automated segmentation could reduce manual workload and improve consistency in 4D Flow MRI-based intracranial hemodynamic analysis.
method: Pretrained a 3D full-resolution nnU-Net on 355 TOF-MRA scans, then fine-tuned it on 11 7T 4D Flow MRI scans.
Compared against two published baselines: a TOF-MRA-only direct-transfer U-Net and a DenseNet U-Net trained from scratch on the 11 4D Flow MRI scans.
Evaluated segmentation quality and effects on area, flow, and wall shear stress against manual reference across test sets with different resolutions.
evidence_signal: The transfer learning nnU-Net achieved Dice scores above 0.85, HD95 around 3 mm, and strong agreement for flow metrics and WSS (ICC up to 0.97), outperforming both comparison models.
watch_item: Results are based on a very small fine-tuning set and some vessel segments still showed significant metric differences versus manual segmentation, so generalization and segment-specific reliability remain concerns.
paper_title: Automated Segmentation of Intracranial Arteries on 4D Flow MRI for Hemodynamic Quantification
